# sqlite-graphrag (v1.2.5 LLM-Only One-Shot)


> Persistent memory for 27 AI agents in a single ~19 MiB Rust binary (LLM-only, one-shot)

27 AI agents. One ~19 MiB binary. Zero model download. **v1.2.2** (crate `1.2.2`, schema **v16**, no main-DB migration; agent-native output surface plus `--no-input`; inherits enrich-queue **CAPA seal**: namespace claim isolation; `--until-empty` op+ns count; `--force-redescribe` reopens skipped/done; re-embed BLOB `LENGTH(embedding)=dim*4` + zombie reconcile; `entity:` enqueue strip; chunk ns validate; CAPA-D compound configuration-file markers; inherits **DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_DIM=1024**) gives every AI coding assistant a local, private memory layer backed by a single SQLite file. Config: **CLI flag > XDG `config set` > default** — product `SQLITE_GRAPHRAG_*` is **not** the config path. E2E seal: help scrub, OpenRouter URLs via XDG, one embedding budget via XDG `embedding.timeout_secs` (default 30s), EntityType fold, remember-batch description required, `pending-embeddings status` / `cache stats`, `purge --now`, `config list --effective`, `related_to`→`related`, telemetry alias removed, `enrich --list-skipped` / `--requeue-skipped`, GAP-SG-139 `--db` no-op on host leaves, `scripts/e2e_offline_v120.sh` **20/20** (historical wrapper `e2e_offline_v118.sh` superseded). Residual honest: residual monólitos optional. Embedding generation is the OpenRouter REST API only (~100-500ms via `--embedding-backend openrouter`); the headless `claude` / `codex` / `opencode` subprocess backends were removed, so `--llm-backend` accepts `openrouter` or `none`. No subprocess, no daemon, no ONNX, no model download. Graph-native retrieval. Deterministic JSON for pipeline orchestration.

- Portuguese version available at [README.pt-BR.md](https://github.com/danilo-aguiar-br/sqlite-graphrag/blob/main/README.pt-BR.md)
- Compact summary in [llms.txt](https://github.com/danilo-aguiar-br/sqlite-graphrag/blob/main/llms.txt); Portuguese variant in [llms.pt-BR.txt](https://github.com/danilo-aguiar-br/sqlite-graphrag/blob/main/llms.pt-BR.txt)

```bash
cargo install --locked sqlite-graphrag
```


## What is it?
### sqlite-graphrag delivers durable memory for AI agents
- Stores memories, entities and relationships inside a single SQLite file (~19 MiB binary)
- Embeds content via OpenRouter REST API (v1.0.93, ~100-500ms) or headless `claude code`, `codex`, `opencode` LLM subprocess (OAuth); the LLM subprocess IS the model
- Combines FTS5 full-text search with pure-Rust cosine KNN over BLOB embeddings into a hybrid Reciprocal Rank Fusion ranker
- `sqlite-vec` extension REMOVED in v1.0.76; cosine similarity is computed in-process over `memory_embeddings` / `entity_embeddings` / `chunk_embeddings` BLOB tables
- Extracts an entity graph with typed edges for multi-hop recall across memories
- Preserves every edit through an immutable version history table for full audit
- Runs on Linux, macOS and Windows natively with zero external services required beyond an LLM CLI on PATH

## v1.0.76 Architecture
- The default build is LLM-only and one-shot. See [ADR-0019](docs/decisions/adr-0019-llm-only-one-shot.md) for the full architectural rationale.
- Daemon: deprecated in v1.0.76 and FULLY REMOVED in v1.0.79 (ahead of the v1.1.0 schedule). The CLI is 100% one-shot with zero IPC; the LLM subprocess is the "model loader".
- `embedding-legacy`, `ner-legacy` and `full` features: REMOVED in v1.0.79 (ahead of the v1.1.0 schedule). The v1.0.74 fastembed + ort + tokenizers + sqlite-vec pipeline no longer exists; every build is LLM-only.
- Embedding pipeline (G42, v1.0.79): default dimensionality 384 (`--embedding-dim`, `SQLITE_GRAPHRAG_EMBEDDING_DIM`, range [8, 4096]; precedence flag > env > `schema_meta.dim` > 384; existing 384-dim databases keep working unchanged); batched LLM calls (calibration bases of 8 chunks / 25 entity names at dim 64, adapted as clamp(base×64/dim, 1, base) — G44); bounded parallelism via `--llm-parallelism` on `remember` (default 4), `ingest` (default 2) and `edit`; `kill_on_drop` plus `SQLITE_GRAPHRAG_EMBED_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 300s) on every subprocess; canonical re-embed via `enrich --operation re-embed` (v1.1.01: `--target memories|entities|chunks|all`) and `edit --force-reembed`; `SQLITE_GRAPHRAG_CLAUDE_EMBED_MODEL` model override.
- Migration from v1.0.74/v1.0.75: `sqlite-graphrag migrate --to-llm-only --drop-vec-tables --db <path>` is the one-shot upgrade. Combines checksum rewrite with V013 vec-table drop.
- OAuth enforcement: the spawn of `claude -p` or `codex exec` ABORTS with `AppError::Validation` if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set in the environment. See [ADR-0025](docs/decisions/adr-0025-oauth-only-embedding.md).
- Cosine similarity is now pure Rust: see [ADR-0020](docs/decisions/adr-0020-pure-rust-cosine.md) for the algorithm. BLOB-backed embeddings replace vec0: see [ADR-0022](docs/decisions/adr-0022-blob-embeddings.md).

## v1.0.86 → v1.0.91 Architecture (Pre-flight, Schema Drift, Flag Parity, OpenCode Backend, Spawn Isolation)
- The pre-flight validation layer (v1.0.87, ADR-0045, GAP-META-005) gates every LLM subprocess spawn BEFORE the fork. `src/spawn/preflight.rs` (≥200 lines, 7 guards, 15 unit tests) runs `check_argv_size`, `check_binary_exists`, `check_mcp_config_inline`, `check_mcp_config_path`, `check_walkup_mcp_json`, `check_output_buffer`, `check_claude_config_dir` before `Command::spawn()`. Failures return `AppError::PreFlightFailed` with `exit_code() == 16` (`EX_CONFIG`, `is_permanent() == true`). Bypass: `SQLITE_GRAPHRAG_SKIP_PREFLIGHT=1`. The 4 spawners (`claude_runner`, `codex_spawn`, `ingest_claude`, `extract/llm_embedding`) share this single module
- v1.0.86 added 10 LLM-pipeline subcommands: `pending list|show|cleanup`, `embedding status|list|abandon`, `pending-embeddings list|process`, `slots status|release`. New global flags: `--max-concurrency`, `--wait-lock`, `--llm-parallelism`, `--ingest-parallelism`, `--graceful-shutdown-secs`, `--skip-embedding-on-failure`. Host-wide slot semaphore via `fs4` with `fcntl(F_SETLK)` on Unix and `LockFileEx` on Windows (ADR-0036-0040)
- v1.0.88 fixed 3 hotfixes: BUG-11 (CRITICAL) preflight failure in `extract/llm_embedding.rs:563-565` now propagates to `remember` via `embed_via_backend_strict`; BUG-12 (MEDIUM) OAuth-only enforcement emits 1 stderr line (was 2); BUG-13 (MEDIUM) `link --create-missing` respects entity-name validation. 11 new regression tests (ADR-0046, ADR-0047)
- v1.0.89 closed 7 GAPs: GAP-E2E-007 `health.schema.json` regenerated via `schemars` derive macro with `additionalProperties: true` (Must-Ignore policy per RFC 7493 I-JSON, 17 new fields); GAP-E2E-008 `--db <PATH>` parity on `embedding status|list|abandon`, `pending list|show`; GAP-E2E-009 `migrate --dry-run --json` reports pending migrations without applying; GAP-E2E-010 `codex-models --json` accepted as no-op; GAP-E2E-011 `ingest --auto-describe` extracts description from first meaningful body line; GAP-E2E-002 `health --namespace <NS> --json` filters counts; GAP-E2E-001 binary size 14.6 MiB documented in `Cargo.toml:6` (ADR-0048, ADR-0049). 1877 tests passing (843 lib + 1013 integration + 21 doc)
- Schema version stays at v15 throughout v1.0.86-91. No database migrations run in this 6-release cycle
- v1.0.90 OpenCode backend integration (ADR-0051, GAP-OPENCODE-001/002): third LLM backend `opencode run` alongside `codex exec` and `claude -p`. New `--llm-backend opencode`, `--mode opencode` for ingest/enrich, `--opencode-binary/model/timeout` flags and `SQLITE_GRAPHRAG_OPENCODE_*` env vars. Fallback chain extended to `codex → claude → opencode → none`. `spawn_opencode()` without RLIMIT_AS (Bun runtime crash fix). 24-bug remediation including `--skip-embedding-on-failure` activation (BUG-SKIP-EMBED), `--llm-fallback` dead-flag fix (GAP-LLM-FALLBACK-DEAD-FLAG), FTS desync in batch/enrich (BUG-BATCH-FTS-DESYNC, BUG-ENRICH-DESC-FTS-DESYNC), Windows cross-compilation (BUG-WINDOWS-001), embedding timeout hardcode (BUG-TIMEOUT-HARDCODE-001), `list` pagination (BUG-LIST-TOTAL-COUNT-001), `--yes` enforcement on 3 destructive commands (BUG-YES-FLAG-IGNORED). 875+ tests passing
- v1.0.91 spawn CWD isolation (GAP-SPAWN-001): `spawn_isolation_dir()` and `apply_cwd_isolation()` in `src/spawn/mod.rs` set `current_dir` to an ephemeral temp directory and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to the same dir for ALL 10 production spawn sites. LLM subprocesses no longer inherit `.mcp.json` from the caller's project — embedding works zero-config in any directory. `cleanup_spawn_dir()` removes the temp dir at process exit (GAP-SPAWN-002). BUG-17 fixed `entities.degree` inflation: `increment_degree()` replaced by `recalculate_degree()` after all relationships are inserted. BUG-15 fixed 7 JSON schemas with missing `"opencode"` and `"auto"` in `backend_invoked` enum. BUG-16 fixed `deep-research.schema.json` missing `vec_degraded` field

## v1.2.2 Patch Notes / Agent-native output surface

- Crate `1.2.2`. NO main-DB schema migration (stays at **v16**). Pin `=1.2.2`. Purely additive: one global output surface plus one global input flag.
- **Eight global output flags**, applied at a single point (`src/agent_surface/`) so one implementation covers the whole CLI: `--select` (alias `--fields`), `--filter`, `--max-items`, `--sort`, `--dedupe-by`, `--count-only`, `--truncate-content`, `--max-output-bytes`.
- **Fixed pipeline order** — filter → sort → dedupe → max-items → select → count-only → truncate-content → max-output-bytes.
- **`--filter` grammar** — `key=value`, `key!=value`, `key~substring` (case-insensitive containment); `==` is a synonym of `=`; repeating the flag conjoins predicates with AND; a malformed expression aborts with **exit 2** so a typo is never mistaken for an empty result set.
- **`--max-items` bounds emission, not retrieval** — distinct from the per-subcommand `--limit` and from `-k`, which bound the query; applied after filtering.
- **`--select` never invents a field** — a key missing from an element is skipped rather than emitted as `null`; dotted paths (`stats.total`) are accepted; an envelope with no result array is projected itself.
- **Failure envelopes are never filtered** — `error: true` / `ok: false` reaches the caller verbatim. `$schema` documents pass through untouched. NDJSON streams bypass the surface entirely, preserving one record per line.
- **Truncation is never silent** — removals are recorded under `agent_surface` (`input_count`, `output_count`, `content_truncated`, `output_truncated`, `dropped`, …) and raise the top-level `truncated` flag. `--truncate-content` counts characters, never bytes, so a UTF-8 sequence is never split; `--max-output-bytes` drops trailing result elements rather than slicing JSON text, which would not parse.
- **Result-array location** — `results`, `items`, `entities`, `memories`, `hits`, `rows`, `matches`, `data`, in that order; otherwise the first array member.
- **`--no-input`** — refuses stdin declaratively: `--body-stdin`, `--graph-stdin`, `remember-batch` and every other stdin reader fail up front with **exit 65**, even when a pipe is attached. Precedence: flag > XDG `cli.no_input` > `false`; disable an XDG opt-in by unsetting the key, never by `--no-input=false`.
- **Precedence for caps** — flag > XDG `agent_surface.max_items` / `agent_surface.truncate_content` / `agent_surface.max_output_bytes` > `0` (disabled). No product environment variable is read.
- With no flag set, the envelope is byte-for-byte identical to v1.2.1 output.
- **New `schema` subcommand** — `sqlite-graphrag schema` emits the catalog of all **75** JSON contracts as NDJSON, one `{"id","invoke"}` per line, where `invoke` is the ready-to-copy command; `sqlite-graphrag schema --name <ID>` emits that contract's JSON Schema document; an unknown `<ID>` exits **4** rather than returning an empty catalog. `--json` does not change the listing, which is NDJSON by definition. Discovering contracts by listing `docs/schemas/` off disk is no longer the source of truth for an agent.
- **`--mode claude-code` NDJSON contract unified (GAP-SG-148 item 5)** — the mode no longer reports through a parallel type: per-file events and the summary use the same `IngestFileEvent` / `IngestSummary` as the standard pipeline. Per-file `status` is **`indexed`** when a memory was written, **not `done`** (full enum `indexed`, `failed`, `skipped`, `preview`); the summary reports **`files_total`, `files_succeeded`, `files_failed`, `files_skipped`**, **not `completed`**. `entities`, `rels` and `cost_usd` are optional members carried by the LLM modes and omitted on the wire by the standard pipeline, so a `--mode none` line stays byte-identical to what it was before the unification.

## v1.2.1 Patch Notes / Enrich queue CAPA seal

- Release 2026-07-31. Crate `1.2.1`. NO main-DB schema migration (stays at **v16**). Pin `=1.2.1`. Sidecar queue behaviour only.
- **Namespace claim isolation** — `dequeue_next_pending`, `count_eligible_pending`, `--resume` / `--retry-failed` require `operation` **and** `namespace`.
- **`--until-empty` counts only this op+namespace** — alien ReEmbed zombies no longer keep other ops spinning with `completed=0`.
- **`--force-redescribe` reopens `skipped`/`done`** — `reopen_force_redescribe_candidates` once per process; never reopens `dead` (use `--requeue-dead`).
- **Re-embed zombie reconciliation** — `reconcile_satisfied_reembed_pending` marks pending done when live vector matches (`LENGTH(embedding) = dim*4`).
- **Re-embed eligibility uses BLOB length** — CORRUPT / META_AHEAD rows (`dim=1024` with 384-d BLOB) still eligible.
- **Enqueue validates re-embed keys** — strip `entity:` for entity lookup; validate chunk keys in target namespace.
- **CAPA-D low-quality markers** — compound "configuration file" phrases only (no bare `%configuration file%` FP).
- Regressions: `enqueue_candidate_accepts_entity_prefixed_reembed_key`, `dequeue_next_pending_isolates_by_namespace`; queue suite 38 OK.

## v1.2.0 Patch Notes / XDG Seal + dim 1024

- Release 2026-07-29. Crate `1.2.0`. NO main-DB schema migration (stays at **v16**). Pin `=1.2.0`. Offline harness `scripts/e2e_offline_v120.sh` **20/20** (historical wrapper `e2e_offline_v118.sh` superseded).
- **DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_DIM=1024** (flag `--embedding-dim` / XDG `embedding.dim` override; existing DBs keep `schema_meta.dim`).
- Config precedence **CLI flag > XDG `config set` > default**; product `SQLITE_GRAPHRAG_*` **not** read at runtime (G-T-XDG-04).
- Enrich queue multi-namespace column + `UNIQUE(namespace, operation, item_key)`; `enrich --list-skipped` / `--requeue-skipped`.
- GAP-SG-139: `--db` documented **no-op** on host/XDG leaves (`config`, `slots`, `cache`, `completions`).
- OpenRouter chat/embeddings URLs resolve from XDG `network.openrouter.chat_url` / `network.openrouter.embeddings_url` (aliases `network.chat_url` / `network.embed_url`).
- Query embed budget: credential probe + XDG `embedding.timeout_secs`, default **30s** (flag `--openrouter-timeout` wins). One budget now governs reads and writes alike; the read-only `llm.probe_timeout_ms` went out with the headless fallback chain it fenced.
- EntityType fold: `map_to_canonical` maps `"module"` → Concept; relation `related_to` → `related`.
- `remember-batch` requires non-empty `description` on create (parity with `remember`).
- UX aliases: `pending-embeddings status` (= `embedding status`), `cache stats` (= `cache list`).
- `purge --now` immediate hard-purge of soft-deletes; `--yes` alone still respects default **90d** retention.
- `config set|get|list|unset`, `config list --effective`, `config doctor`, `config path`, `config add-key`.
- Help scrub: no product env tables / no Box about on ingest/enrich; telemetry lib alias removed.
- Residual honest: GAP-SG-89 LOC≤800 largely closed; residual monólitos optional; live LQ entity-description backfill is an operator campaign.

## v1.1.06 Patch Notes

- Release 2026-07-12. Official name v1.1.06; crate `1.1.6`. NO schema migration (v16). Pin library consumers `=1.1.6`.
- Closes GAP-ENTITY-CONNECT-SCAN-CARTESIAN (P0 hang on large `global`): O(k) pair scan via co-occurrence in `memory_entities` + hub × degree-0 island fill (never cartesian `entities × entities` with global ORDER BY).
- Queue keys `pair:{id1}:{id2}`, `item_type=entity_pair`; drain by primary key without re-scan. GAP-002 `entity_connect_seen` (v1.1.04) preserved.

- NDJSON: `phase: scan_start` before SQL with real `operation` (`entity-connect` or `cross-domain-bridges`), `entities_in_namespace`, `backlog_degree0_proxy`; `scan_meta` with `pairs_enqueued_this_scan` / `scan_elapsed_ms`.
- `cross-domain-bridges` shares the same fully-implemented O(k) path.
- Suite: `tests/v1106_entity_connect_scan_regression.rs` + unit tests in enrich. ADR-0066.

## v1.1.05 Patch Notes

- Release 2026-07-11. Official release name is v1.1.05; the crate manifest carries `version = "1.1.5"` because the SemVer parser rejects a leading zero in the patch component. NO schema migration — schema stays at v16 from v1.1.04. Library consumers pin `=1.1.5`. Integration suite: `tests/v1105_danilo_bugs_regression.rs`.
- Bug 1 (Fixed): `deep-research` single-token queries (e.g. `"danilo"`) expand to multi-aspect sub-queries with `source: "aspect"` covering patrimony, stack, stakeholders, projects, decisions, relationships and context (EN/PT facets). Manual strategy remains available via `--sub-query-strategy manual --sub-queries-file`.
- Bug 2 (Added): `deep-research --output PATH` writes the full envelope via the atomwrite algorithm (tempfile same dir → fsync → rename) and emits a short stdout ack with `blake3` checksum (`written`, `bytes`, `blake3`, ...). Global `--quiet`/`-q` suppresses non-error tracing. Stdout is JSON; stderr is logs — never mix with `&>`.
- Bug 3 (Added): `graph traverse --fuzzy` auto-resolves a clear single short-name winner (stderr warning); without `--fuzzy`, NotFound (exit 4) includes ranked Jaro-Winkler / prefix suggestions of canonical names (`rapidfuzz`).
- Bug 4 (Fixed): `merge-entities` rejects self-referential merges (`--ids` containing `--into-id`, or `--names` containing `--into`) BEFORE any DB work, so shell word-splitting mistakes cannot corrupt the graph under `--cross-namespace`.
- Bug 5 (Added): `link --from-id` / `--to-id` resolve by entity ID; `validate_entity_name` rejects digit-only names so `--create-missing` cannot create ghost numeric entities.

## v1.1.04 Patch Notes

- Release 2026-07-08. Official release name is v1.1.04; the crate manifest carries `version = "1.1.4"` because the SemVer parser rejects a leading zero in the patch component. Database migration REQUIRED — `migrate --json` applies V016. Schema advances v15→v16.
- GAP-001 (Fixed): `deep-research` no longer panics with "Cannot start a runtime from within a runtime". The sync entry point now computes per-sub-query embeddings BEFORE building its dedicated Tokio runtime (new `compute_sub_embeddings` helper in `deep_research.rs`), and the three OpenRouter embedding paths in `embedder.rs` (single, serial batch, JoinSet fan-out) adopt the canonical `Handle::try_current` + `block_in_place` reentry pattern already used by the batch path. `ingest_opencode` is also guarded against nested-runtime panics for any future caller running inside an existing runtime.
- GAP-002 (Fixed): `entity-connect` now converges. A new `entity_connect_seen` table (migration V016) records the LLM verdict (`related`/`none`) for each evaluated pair, the `scan_isolated_entity_pairs` scanner excludes already-evaluated pairs and prioritises hub entities, `count_operation_backlog` reports a real O(n) backlog proxy (degree-0 entities with NER bindings) instead of a hard-coded zero, and `call_entity_connect` persists the verdict on both the `related` and `none` branches. `--until-empty` now reaches `eligible_remaining == 0` instead of re-evaluating the same rejected pairs forever.
- Migration V016 (Added): `entity_connect_seen(source_id, target_id, namespace, verdict, relation, evaluated_at)` with composite primary key `(source_id, target_id)`, dual `ON DELETE CASCADE` foreign keys to `entities(id)`, a `verdict` check constraint, and a namespace index. `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` advances from 15 to 16.
- Docs: the `entity-connect` enrich operation is promoted from "scan-only (does not persist)" to "fully-implemented" in the skill reference.


## v1.1.03 Patch Notes
- Release 2026-07-07. Official release name is v1.1.03; the crate manifest carries `version = "1.1.3"` because the SemVer parser rejects a leading zero in the patch component. No main schema migration (v15); the enrich sidecar queue gains a `claimed_at` column via idempotent ALTER.
- Bug 1 (Fixed): the enrich scan-enqueue path now batches candidate inserts in a single transaction instead of row-by-row under the WAL write lock, eliminating the apparent scan-phase deadlock that froze the 44 163-entity `re-embed --target entities` workload under stale-claim contention.
- Bug 2 (Added): `reclassify-relation` gains `--literal-to <RELATION>` (verbatim target write) complementing `--literal-from`; `--literal-from applies_to --literal-to applies_to --batch` migrates the 61 357 legacy underscore edges (`applies_to`, `depends_on`, `tracked_in`) to canonical hyphen form.
- Bug 3 (Added): `merge-entities` gains `--cross-namespace` (opt-in, default same-namespace) so `--ids`/`--into-id` resolve across all namespaces.
- Bug 4 (Added): the enrich sidecar gains a `claimed_at` column, stale `processing` claims are reset on startup, a SIGTERM handler performs graceful cleanup before exit 19, and `enrich --reset-stale-claims` plus `enrich --stale-claim-secs <N>` manually clear stale processing claims.
- Bug 5 (Docs): the `enrich --status` help text clarifies that `scan_backlog` is the REAL pending work, `queue_pending` is a COMPUTED COUNT, `eligible_now == 0` with `queue_pending > 0` is COOLDOWN, and `eligible_now > 0` stuck against `state: "draining"` is a deadlock recoverable via `--reset-stale-claims`.
- Bug 6 (Fixed): the `re-embed --target chunks` scanner and `count_operation_backlog` switch from `JOIN memories` to `LEFT JOIN memories` so chunks of soft-deleted mothers reach a real 100% coverage.
- V8 (Added): new `split-body` subcommand divides memories whose body exceeds 25 000 characters into daughter memories at chunk boundaries, marks the original superseded, and creates `replaces` relations from each daughter to the original. Daughters are not embedded inline; run `enrich --operation re-embed --target memories` afterwards.

## v1.1.02 Patch Release
- Release 2026-07-06. Official release name is v1.1.02; the crate manifest carries `version = "1.1.2"` because the SemVer parser rejects a leading zero in the patch component. No schema migration (v15). The OpenRouter clients send User-Agent `sqlite-graphrag/1.1.2` derived from CARGO_PKG_VERSION. Release binary approximately 19 MiB.
- Gap 1 (Removed, BREAKING): the `--gliner-variant` argument is dropped from `remember` and `ingest` — since the GLiNER NER pipeline removal in v1.0.79 it survived as a silent no-op (exit 0); clap now rejects it with exit 2; the dead GLiNER plumbing in constants.rs/extraction.rs is deleted; tests/gliner_variant_removed_regression.rs guards both subcommands.
- Gap 2 (Fixed): the embedding token ceiling raises `AppError::TooManyTokens { tokens, limit }` (exit 6 preserved, PT-BR message via i18n), validated at the write boundary of `remember`/`remember-batch`/`edit` and inside the shared embedding client (`embedding_api`), which also covers `ingest`.
- Gap 3 (Added, regression coverage): tests/reembed_entities_integration.rs guards the re-embed entity dispatch fix landed in v1.1.01 (`strip_prefix("entity:")` dispatch to `call_reembed_entity`).
- Added: `enrich --prune-dead-entity-orphans` — dedicated flag to prune `status='dead' AND item_type='entity'` rows from the queue sidecar, complementing the memory-scoped `--prune-dead-orphans`.
- 4 pre-existing rustdoc warnings resolved (backticks escaping HTML tags in doc-comments; removal of broken intra-doc links to cfg(test) methods).

## v1.1.01 Architecture (12-Priority gaps.md Roadmap Closure)
- Release 2026-07-02. Official release name is v1.1.01; the crate manifest carries `version = "1.1.1"` because the SemVer parser rejects a leading zero in the patch component. No schema migration (v15). The OpenRouter clients send User-Agent `sqlite-graphrag/1.1.1` derived from CARGO_PKG_VERSION. Release binary approximately 19 MiB
- P1: entity vectors are no longer silently skipped at write time — with `--embedding-backend openrouter` the entity-embedding chain resolves to `[OpenRouter]` even under `--llm-backend none` (REST, no subprocess), and an empty vector never persists a row: `upsert_entity_vec`, `upsert_chunk_vec` and `memories::upsert_vec` gain an empty-embedding guard so vector-less items stay visible to the re-embed backfill instead of being masked by an empty BLOB
- P2: retroactive embedding backfill via `enrich --operation re-embed --target memories|entities|chunks|all` (default `memories`, fully retro-compatible). New scanners for entities/chunks without a live vector in `src/commands/enrich/scan.rs`, queue keys prefixed `entity:`/`chunk:` with per-key `item_type`, prefix dispatch inside `call_reembed`, and `count_operation_backlog` reports the `scan_backlog` per target in `--status` (GAP-SG-77 parity preserved via shared predicates)
- P3: `graph recompute-degree` (in `src/commands/graph_export.rs`) reconciles the cached `entities.degree` with the real edge counts in one IMMEDIATE transaction, per namespace (or all), with `--dry-run` and the envelope `{namespace, dry_run, total, updated, zeroed, unchanged, elapsed_ms}`. Semantics match the canonical `recalculate_degree` helper (self-loop counts once)
- P4: `reclassify-relation --literal-from` matches the stored relation VERBATIM (no hyphen→underscore normalization at the clap boundary), making legacy hyphenated edges (e.g. `applies-to`) reachable; mutually exclusive with `--from-relation`, and the from==to guard compares the raw literal against the normalized `--to-relation` so `--literal-from applies-to --to-relation applies_to` is a valid migration
- P5: ID-based disambiguation for entity maintenance — `merge-entities --ids/--into-id` and `rename-entity --id`, namespace-scoped, so duplicated names across namespaces stop blocking merges/renames
- P6: real coverage observability — `health --json` gains `vec_memories_missing`, `vec_entities_missing`, `vec_chunks_missing` and the per-table `vec_*_coverage_pct` fields; `embedding status --json` gains the per-table `*_missing` counters
- P7: `EntityType` deserialization is a manual `Deserialize` with a rich boundary error (13 valid values + hints) surfaced as a Validation error (exit 1) with early validation in `--graph-stdin`/`remember --entities-file`, instead of a bare serde/Json error (exit 20); canonical vocabularies (entity types, relations) and namespace semantics are documented
- P10: the re-embed predicates (`reembed_*_predicate` in `scan.rs`) select rows whose stored `dim` diverges from the configured `--embedding-dim` — or whose blob is empty — across all three vector tables (`memory_embeddings`, `entity_embeddings`, `chunk_embeddings`); legacy-dimension vectors are finally regenerated
- P11: the byte/chunk ceilings raise typed errors with actionable context: `AppError::BodyTooLarge { bytes, limit }` and `AppError::TooManyChunks { chunks, limit }` (exit 6 preserved, PT-BR messages via `i18n`) replace `LimitExceeded` at every body-size call site (`remember`, `edit`, `ingest`, `enrich` prompt template)
- P12: `ingest --name-prefix <PREFIX>` applies a kebab-case prefix to every derived memory name, with the derived-part budget shrunk so `prefix + derived` always respects the 80-char name cap

## v1.1.0 Architecture (Enrich Dead-Letter Root Fixes, GAP-SG-70..78)
- Truncated OpenRouter completions no longer dead-letter: `chat_api` deserializes `choices[].finish_reason` and, on `"length"`, re-emits the request with a grown `max_tokens` (bounded by `ENRICH_MAX_LENGTH_RETRIES`) before attempting JSON repair (GAP-SG-70)
- Retry classification is fully TYPED by `AppError` variant — no message-substring matching; non-JSON responses and not-yet-materialized entities are Transient (retried), only real permanent failures (validation/args) go straight to `dead` (GAP-SG-73/78). `--list-dead` gains `finish_reason`/`input_tokens`/`output_tokens` diagnostics (GAP-SG-72)
- `enrich --status` gains `scan_backlog` (real database candidates per operation using the same WHERE predicates as the scanners), eliminating the false `pending=0` on `entity-descriptions`/`body-enrich`/`re-embed` (GAP-SG-77); the dequeue loop uses `busy_timeout` + bounded retry and fails loudly with exit 15 under sustained `SQLITE_BUSY` contention (GAP-SG-76). The OpenRouter HTTP client is de-duplicated into a shared module. Schema stays v15 (idempotent ALTER adds diagnostic queue columns)

## v1.0.99 Architecture (Remove Destructive Degree-Cap Pruning + Doc/Convergence Fixes, ADR-0059, GAP-SG-67/68/69)
- GAP-SG-67 (ADR-0059): the destructive GLOBAL degree-cap pruning is removed — `graph::enforce_degree_cap` and its two call sites (`remember`, `link`) are deleted, and the `--max-entity-degree` flag is removed from both commands. BREAKING: passing `--max-entity-degree` is rejected by clap (exit 2); the prior `--max-entity-degree 0` mitigation is obsolete. Writes are now 100% additive — they never prune/delete edges nor emit a warn, and the total `relationships` count never decreases on a normal write. Schema stays v15 (no migration). Trade-off: hub degree grows unbounded; future normalisation is an explicit MAINTENANCE command only
- GAP-SG-68: `graph entities --sort-by degree` sorted ascending against a doc-comment that promised "descending by default"; the fix aligns the DOC to the ascending behaviour ("Sort by degree (total number of relationships). Use --order desc for most-connected-first."). Only `src/commands/graph_export.rs` (one line) changed; the 6 `build_order_by_*` tests stay green
- GAP-SG-69: `enrich --operation body-enrich --until-empty` did not converge because the scan re-scanned bodies the preservation guard rejected (status `skipped`). Fix: the `skipped_item_keys` helper (`queue.rs`) lets the BodyEnrich initial scan + rescan exclude preservation-vetoed `skipped` keys, the `.enrich-queue.sqlite` sidecar is preserved while `skipped` rows remain (removed only when `dead==0` AND `skipped==0`), and `cleanup_queue_entry` clears the veto when the body changes. Empirical convergence 55->3; test `skipped_item_keys_excludes_only_skipped_for_operation`
- New ADR-0059 (EN + PT-BR); docs/decisions/INDEX.md updated. No schema migration (v15)

## v1.0.97 Architecture (Enrich Dead-Letter Recovery + Write Ergonomics, GAP-20, SG-32)
- Enrich dead-letter recovery: `--requeue-dead` moves terminal `dead` items back to `pending` for another pass, `--list-dead` emits a read-only JSON listing of each dead item with its `error_class` and `message`, `--ignore-backoff` dequeues eligible items immediately bypassing the `next_retry_at` cooldown, and `--prune-dead-orphans` is a read-only inspector (no LLM, no singleton) that deletes `dead` memory-type queue entries whose `item_key` no longer exists in the main database, leaving entity rows untouched — only the sidecar `.enrich-queue.sqlite` is mutated, the JSON `DeadSummary` gains a `pruned` field, cleans orphaned dead-letter from renamed/purged memories (GAP-SG-66, ADR-0058). There is no in-place reset of the queue file
- Enrich inspectors decoupled from the LLM path: `--status`, `--list-dead`, `--requeue-dead` and `--prune-dead-orphans` now run WITHOUT `--operation`/`--mode` (previously `--mode` was mandatory and omitting it exited 2). New operation `augment-bindings` adds bindings to memories that are ALREADY linked and REQUIRES `--names`/`--names-file`; `body-extract --body-extract-graph-only` extracts the graph read-only without rewriting the body
- Defaults raised: `--max-attempts` default is now 8 (range 1..=20); `--openrouter-timeout` default is now 600s. The enrich queue still lives in the sidecar `.enrich-queue.sqlite`; the per-namespace singleton is unchanged, with `--rest-concurrency` (clamp 1..=16, default 8) as the throughput remedy (GAP-20)
- `remember` write ergonomics: `--graph-file <path>` loads the entity graph from a file (combinable with `--body-file`), `--strict-name` rejects a non-kebab name instead of normalizing it, and `--replace-graph` (with `--force-merge`) zeroes the existing entity/relationship bindings before writing the new graph
- `ingest --force-merge` updates duplicate files instead of skipping them; dedup is by `body_hash` (an unchanged file is skipped even after a rename); oversized bodies are auto-split natively into chunks. `read --format raw` prints the pure body with no JSON envelope. `unlink --memory <name> --entity <name>` removes a single curated memory-to-entity binding without touching entity-to-entity edges
- `embedding status --json` adds a `coverage` object reporting the real vector counts per table; `stats --json` exposes a top-level `total_memories`. `--db <PATH>` must be placed AFTER the subcommand (v1.1.8: product env is not the config path; use flag or XDG). Historical note for v1.0.97 era: schema stayed at v15

## v1.0.96 Architecture (Enrich Dead-Letter + REST Concurrency, ADR-0055)
- `enrich --until-empty` runs an internal scan->drain loop until the eligible queue empties or `--max-runtime` (default 3600s) expires, replacing the external bash drain loop (GAP-ENRICH-BACKLOG-CONVERGE)
- Dead-letter queue: the `.enrich-queue.sqlite` queue gains `error_class` and `next_retry_at` columns via idempotent `ALTER TABLE`, a terminal `dead` status, and the `idx_enrich_queue_eligible ON queue(status, next_retry_at)` index. Classification reuses `AttemptOutcome` + `compute_delay` from `src/retry.rs`: Transient failures (rate-limit, timeout, 5xx) schedule `next_retry_at` with exponential backoff; HardFailures (validation, parse) go terminal at once; an item turns `dead` after `--max-attempts` (default 5, range 1..=20) Transient retries OR on the first HardFailure. Dequeue honours `next_retry_at` and excludes `dead`, so the live set is strictly decreasing
- New flags: `--until-empty`, `--max-runtime <SECONDS>` (default 3600), `--max-attempts <N>` (default 5, 1..=20), `--status` (read-only JSON report of `unbound_backlog`, `queue_pending/done/failed/dead/skipped`, `eligible_now`, `waiting` — calls NO LLM, acquires NO singleton), `--rest-concurrency <N>` (clamp 1..=16, default 8, DISTINCT from `--llm-parallelism`)
- REST fan-out (GAP-OPENROUTER-REST-CONCURRENCY): `embed_passages_parallel_with_embedding_choice` in `src/embedder.rs` fans out the OpenRouter REST calls per 32-chunk batch with a bounded `tokio::task::JoinSet` (NO new dependency); chunk order is preserved by index and in-flight is clamped 1..16 (Cloudflare-safe range). SQLite writes stay serialized via WAL + atomic claim (single-writer intact). Order proof (live test): diagonal cosine 0.9999, off-diagonal max 0.899, argmax 64/64
- New schema `docs/schemas/enrich-status.schema.json` (DERIVED per ADR-0048; regenerated via `dump_schema`, never hand-edited). New ADR-0055 (EN + PT-BR); docs/decisions/INDEX.md updated
- Tests: 8 dead-letter unit tests in `commands::enrich::tests`, 1 ordering test in `embedder::tests` (`reassemble_ordered_restores_input_order`), live `tests/openrouter_live_concurrency.rs` (`#[ignore]`, run with `--ignored`); nextest 1086 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped

## v1.0.95 Architecture (OpenRouter Chat Enrich, ADR-0054, GAP-OR-ENRICH)
- `enrich --mode openrouter` routes the enrich JUDGE to the OpenRouter REST `/chat/completions` endpoint; structured extraction (memory-bindings, entity-descriptions, body-enrich) no longer requires a local claude/codex/opencode CLI
- New flags: `--openrouter-model` (REQUIRED, no default, exit 1 when absent), `--openrouter-api-key` (XDG `config add-key`; product env `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is ignored at runtime), `--openrouter-timeout` (default 300), `--openrouter-base-url` (optional). New module `src/chat_api.rs` (`OpenRouterChatClient`) mirrors `src/embedding_api.rs`; the SCAN->JUDGE->PERSIST pipeline is unchanged — only the JUDGE transport moves
- Structured Outputs strict mode plus `provider.require_parameters`; `reasoning.enabled:false` with a reasoning-mandatory fallback path; `usage.cost` is read from the response. 13/13 OpenRouter text models compatible (9 with `reasoning.enabled:false`, 4 via the reasoning-mandatory fallback)

## v1.0.94 Architecture (Four-Gap Remediation, ADR-0053)
- Default embedding dimension raised from 64 to 384 (`constants.rs`); fresh `init` stamps `dim=384`; legacy 64-dim databases preserved via `schema_meta.dim`
- `enrich --mode` is REQUIRED and its only accepted value is `openrouter`; omitting it is rejected with clap exit 2
- Entity embedding in `remember`/`remember-batch`/`ingest` honours `--embedding-backend`/`--llm-backend`; `remember` with new entities drops from ~119s to ~0.9s under OpenRouter
- Embedding subprocess timeout raised from 120s to 300s

## v1.0.93 Architecture (OpenRouter Embedding Backend)
- v1.0.93 adds optional OpenRouter REST API embedding backend via `--embedding-backend auto|openrouter|llm` global flag (ADR-0052, GAP-OR-INGEST)
- `EmbeddingBackendChoice` enum (`Auto`, `Openrouter`, `Llm`) is separate from `LlmBackendChoice` — embedding backend selection is independent of LLM backend for extraction/enrichment
- `--embedding-model MODEL` selects the OpenRouter model; NO default — user MUST specify when using `--embedding-backend openrouter`
- API key: `--openrouter-api-key` flag or XDG `config add-key openrouter` (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is ignored at runtime; handled via `secrecy::SecretString` with zeroize-on-drop, NEVER logged)
- Direct REST API via `reqwest+rustls-tls` to `POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/embeddings` — ~100-500ms vs 20-60s subprocess LLM cold-start
- MRL (Matryoshka Representation Learning) truncation to configured `--embedding-dim` (default 384); `dimensions` parameter sent when the model supports MRL
- 10 verified models: `qwen/qwen3-embedding-4b`, `qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b`, `nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-vl-1b-v2:free`, `openai/text-embedding-3-small`, `openai/text-embedding-3-large`, `perplexity/pplx-embed-v1-0.6b`, `mistralai/mistral-embed-2312`, `baai/bge-m3`, `google/gemini-embedding-001`, `google/gemini-embedding-2`
- `EmbeddingBackendChoice` propagated to ALL 8 embedding commands: `remember`, `remember-batch`, `ingest`, `recall`, `edit`, `restore`, `hybrid-search`, `deep-research`
- `--enrich-after` flag on `ingest` triggers `enrich --operation memory-bindings` sequentially after all files are ingested
- BUG-OR-1 (input_type per model), BUG-OR-2 (MRL detection), BUG-OR-3 (model validation), BUG-OR-4 (HTTP 200 malformed retry), BUG-OR-5 (dimension override)
- New modules: `src/embedding_api.rs` (OpenRouter client), `src/config.rs` (TOML config), `src/commands/config_cmd.rs` (config subcommand)
- New test file: `tests/openrouter_embedding.rs` (E2E tests with `wiremock` for HTTP mocking)


## Why sqlite-graphrag?
### Differentiators against cloud RAG stacks
- Offline-first architecture eliminates OpenAI embeddings and Pinecone recurring fees
- Single-file SQLite storage replaces Docker clusters of vector databases entirely
- Graph-native retrieval beats pure vector RAG on multi-hop questions by design
- Deterministic JSON output unlocks clean orchestration by LLM agents in pipelines
- Native cross-platform binary ships without Python, Node or Docker dependencies
- Remove recurring cloud vector database dependencies from local agent workflows
- Keep retrieval local to the workstation or CI runner instead of a remote RAG stack


## Economy That Converts
### Numbers That Sell The Switch
- Graph traversal can reduce repeated prompt stuffing in agent loops
- Batched, parallel LLM embedding calls (v1.0.79) collapse dozens of subprocess spawns into a handful per memory
- Single-file storage lowers the operational surface compared to a remote RAG stack
- Your proprietary data NEVER leaves the developer workstation or the CI runner
- Your compliance surface shrinks to one SQLite file under your own encryption
- Your audit trail lives in the `memory_versions` table with immutable history


## Quick Start
### Install and record your first memory in four commands
```bash
cargo install --locked sqlite-graphrag
sqlite-graphrag init
sqlite-graphrag remember --name onboarding-note --type user --description "first memory" --body "hello graphrag"
sqlite-graphrag recall "graphrag" --k 5 --json
```
- The flag `--locked` reuses the `Cargo.lock` shipped with the crate to prevent MSRV breakage
- Without `--locked` Cargo may resolve a patch release that requires a newer `rustc` than 1.88


## Superpowers for AI Agents
### First-class CLI contract for orchestration
- Every subcommand accepts `--json` producing deterministic stdout payloads
- Every invocation is stateless and one-shot — there is no daemon to manage (removed in v1.0.79)
- Every write is idempotent through `--name` kebab-case uniqueness constraints
- Stdin is explicit: use `--body-stdin` for body text or `--graph-stdin` for one `{body?, entities, relationships}` object; raw entity and relationship arrays use `--entities-file` and `--relationships-file`
- `remember` accepts body payloads up to `512000` bytes and up to `512` chunks
- Stderr carries tracing output under `SQLITE_GRAPHRAG_LOG_LEVEL=debug` only
- Cross-platform behavior is identical across Linux, macOS and Windows hosts
